findings.description: The critical-area routing list was not updated for the new `src/core/enums/` files, so enum members that were critical-area types now route as standard.
findings.body:
**`CRITICAL_AREAS` doesn't cover the enums this PR moved out of critical files.**

This PR moves five value sets out of files that `CRITICAL_AREAS` covers and into `src/core/enums/`. No glob in the list matches that folder.

| New file | Came from | Glob that covered it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/core/enums/sandbox-mode.enums.ts` | `src/core/types/sandbox.types.ts` | `'src/core/types/sandbox*'` |
| `src/core/enums/interrupt-signal.enums.ts` | `src/core/types/sandbox.types.ts` | `'src/core/types/sandbox*'` |
| `src/core/enums/merge-status.enums.ts` | `src/core/types/merge-gate.types.ts` | `'src/core/types/merge-gate*'` |
| `src/core/enums/gate-stage-status.enums.ts` | `src/core/types/merge-gate.types.ts` | `'src/core/types/merge-gate*'` |
| `src/core/enums/event-type.enums.ts` | `src/core/types/session.types.ts` | explicit entry |

In `globTokens`, `*` doesn't match `/`. So `'src/core/sandbox*'` and the other root-level patterns can't reach into `src/core/enums/`.

**What goes wrong:** `tierForScope` tiers a task `standard` when its scope-in names only these enum files. That task gets the weaker review and model tier, even though it changes sandbox, merge-gate or event-store values.

**Why it's required:** the doc comment on the list says so (lines 14-17):

> a future extraction out of a critical file needs its own entry here, and its path added to the routing test's list, which pins only the paths it names.

ADR 0092 (amended in #413) says the same: "a file moved out of a critical area stays critical." The routing test only pins the paths it names, so nothing fails today.

**Fix:**
- Add the five paths to `CRITICAL_AREAS`.
- Add the same five paths to the critical-path list in `src/core/routing-utils.test.ts` (around line 81).
- Update the comment so its `{types,constants,errors}` list also includes `enums`.

The other new enums came from non-critical files and need no entry: `climb-reason`, `baseline-stage-status`, `origin-recording`, `debt-metric`, `stage-delta`, `session-activity-kind` and `slot-holder-kind`.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/05818eb9763a1cbcfd261f1aae22cf10b3e7f420/src/core/routing.utils.ts#L10-L47>

findings.description: The only tests that `pup plan add|edit --tier critical` is accepted and stored now type the argv word and the expected value as `Tier.Critical`, so a later change to the enum value would pass them while refusing the documented `--tier critical` word.

`ClimbReason | 'blocked' | undefined` keeps a bare `'blocked'` literal beside the new enum (also session-lifecycle.service.ts:362,435 and dashboard.service.ts:309-310). general.md §Code layout bans bare strings compared at the use site, so use `MergeStatus.Blocked` or give the sentinel its own member.

`commandStage` now checks `stage !== GateStage.Test && stage !== NestedPackageStage.Test`, but both members are `'test'`. A reader has to work out that the second check is redundant; one comparison would do.

The SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP triple is written out by hand in three places: here (now a six-line `||` chain), `LOCK_SIGNALS` in merge-gate.service.ts and `INTERRUPTS` in land-batch.service.ts. `Object.values(InterruptSignal)` would define it once.
`passingAdapter` hand-lists `[GateStage.Build, GateStage.Test, GateStage.Lint]` across six lines; `Object.values(GateStage)` is shorter and stays correct if a stage is added.

process_issues.description: The simplicity reviewer's `git diff` on src/adapters and src/claude failed with a bwrap error (`Can't get type of source .git/config.worktree.lock`), so it did not read those diffs or the test-file diffs. The correctness and security reviewers did cover those paths. One correctness instance hit the same error once, and a retry worked.

The conventions reviewer's leftover-literal grep was capped by head_limit and did not cover multi-line `as const` arrays, so the scan is not exhaustive. A correctness instance separately noted an unconverted `['merge', 'landed', 'retired'].includes(row.type)` at src/core/fix-round.service.ts:934. It behaves the same at runtime, but the PR's acceptance criteria say no such literal should remain.
